audit.whatIsWrong: Every phases[N].side read 'Yasuo' while the content layer and the packet both read Hwei/Hwei/Hwei/Skill/Skill/Hwei/Hwei — the page gave two different answers to every row.
audit.why: Hwei's paints all outrange Steel Tempest (475) and Sweeping Blade (475), and the matchup runs 52.87% over 3531 games; the two agreeing layers describe the lane correctly.
audit.corrected: Full layer moved onto the content chart: Hwei at 1-3, Skill at 4-5 and 6, Hwei at first item and two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes were written around 'crit items' with no Yasuo cooldown anywhere, so the windows were not actionable.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s and is the only cooldown in his kit long enough to plan around — Sweeping Blade resets off minions at 0.5s and Steel Tempest is a flat 4s.
audit.corrected: Every window now keyed to Wind Wall's 25s rank-1 cooldown and its 4-second duration.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said 'his Wind Wall only blocks a single spell, not your full combo' in spikes[0].text, early and wants.foe[2]. That is false and it is the single most important interaction in the matchup.
audit.why: Riot's text: Wind Wall 'creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds', and the kit flags every one of Hwei's abilities — Q, W, E and R — as a projectile. It blanks the entire palette, not one spell. His passive also builds a shield while he moves, so the first paint that lands is often absorbed.
audit.corrected: Bait Wind Wall with the cheapest paint, then commit inside its 25-second rank-1 downtime; expect the first paint of any all-in to be eaten by the moving shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: Wind Wall 25s at rank 1 down to 17s, Sweeping Blade 0.5s, Last Breath 70/50/30s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles.
audit.why: Lint flagged both; the titles promise dash-punishing and fear discipline and the bodies described generic trading.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to their own titles using Sweeping Blade's 0.5s reset.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — the palette stops costing you the lane. Poke the wave contact, mark, detonate, reset.

edits.after: Spiraling Despair is a projectile the wall eats, and Last Breath only needs one knockup — level 6 cuts both ways.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E fear paint like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1, 17s at rank 5, and for 4 seconds it blanks every projectile you own — bait it, then paint the whole downtime. - Sweeping Blade resets every 0.5s off minions, so his gap-close is never the cooldown you count.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by walling your paints, riding the wave to you with Sweeping Blade, and turning one knockup into Last Breath.

edits.before: Standing mid-cast-animation inside his engage range with the fear already spent — every assassin and fighter in the pool is waiting for exactly that frame.
edits.after: Painting into a Yasuo who has stopped moving — Wind Wall eats the projectile, he dashes the caster minions to you, and the second Steel Tempest knocks you up.

edits.before: Carry through range — no mid pool champion paints a teamfight from further away; your R + QQ decides objectives before they start.

edits.after: If Yasuo gets a kill, never paint while he is standing still — that is the wall going down. Two kills: farm with QA clears from outside 475 and step up only on Wind Wall's 25s cooldown.

edits.before: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Bait it, count it, then go.
